results.name: VHF Skull Point Cloud
results.description:
A skull point cloud generated from a CT scan of the [Visible Human Female](https://www.nlm.nih.gov/research/visible/animations.html) downloaded from [here](https://mri.radiology.uiowa.edu/visible_human_datasets.html).

CT .nrrd volume generated with 3D Slicer was imported into Paraview. A color ramp was applied and the volume was "clipped" to the voxels representing mostly bone then converted to a point cloud. Meshlab was used to clean up extraneous points. The volume of point clouds looks similar to the volume rendering in CT software but can be rendered in Sketchfab.

YouTube video explaining the process: https://youtu.be/00JkLcklOpc.

results.name: Bailey Bridge DD type
results.description:
Model of a panel bridge with wooden deck, Bailey type DD based on M2 version.

The model of the bridge is consisted of three objects, the Male Ramp, the Bay section and the Female Ramp. All of them are “Children” of the Empty DD_StartPoint.

The placement of the bridge starts allways from the Male Ramp and then follows the 10 feet Bay section, wich it has an Array Modifier so you can increases the span 10ft each time.

The DD type can reach 180ft span, so every 10 feet there is a corresponding empty for Female Ramp to be attached.

Ramps are two type single length and double lenght.

results.name: A teenager's dream
results.description:
My final entry for the skateboard texturing challenge.

Although I would probably hang it on my wall today, this skateboard has all the features I would have dreamt of as a teenager:

* Sick natural engraving design inspired by Sin City
* DC comics "collector edition" trucks
* Old Spitfire wheels
* 8 plys of Canadian maple: who needs flex anyway?
* The obvious griptape logo ;)
* Random surf/skate sticker
* Tony Hawk signature
* And to prove I'm not a poser, I even wore it by riding it to a few sessions at the park! 

The materials were entirely (and sometimes painfully) created within Gimp and Blender, and the final textures were baked for export with [BakeMyScan](http://bakemyscan.org). 

Matcap+Surface should give you a better view of some details!

![Imgur](https://i.imgur.com/08TbHTm.jpg)

Based on "[Skateboard (Sketchfab Texturing Challenge)](https://sketchfab.com/models/cc02ca24d04147e29c0942830f74affc)" by [Johnson Martin](https://sketchfab.com/Johnson-Martin), licensed under CC Attribution-ShareAlike.

results.name: Polybios
results.description:
Statue of Polybios at the entrance ramp of the parliament building in the 1st district of Vienna. The statue was made in 1899 by Alois Düll.

Polybios was an ancient Greek historian who became famous for his main work, the partially preserved Historíai. In it he describes in originally 40 books the universal history of Rome over the period from the beginning of the First Punic War to the destruction of Carthage and Corinth.

results.name: Half-Life MAV-88 Osprey
results.description:
Half-Life Osprey VTOL made for [an Arma 3 mod](https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2560124474).

Box modelled from scratch in Blender, textured in Substance Painter.

Very happy with this one. It's a combination of the three versions of the Osprey found in HL1 and Opposing Force. The first of OPFOR's is the same as HL1, only with landing gear and a ramp, and the other is the interior used for the cutscenes.

The problem is that the interior has a completely different door design than the other two, and it also lacks any windows despite both other models indicating it should. I decided to do the cutscene door design, include the windows, and redesign the ramp to maintain the OG hull's look. The red lights are modelled, but their light isn't baked.

Fun fact: the two character code on the tail of military aircraft is a base/unit code. Assuming all Ospreys we see in HL1 either come from Santego or are owned by the HECU, A3 is either the base code for Santego, or the unit code for the HECU.
